questions.question: In a classroom experiment, students use tweezers to pick up green and white cocktail sticks scattered on green grass. What is this simple model demonstrating?
options: How photosynthesis works in plants
Natural selection based on camouflage
The rate of fossilisation in different soils
How human muscles grow stronger with exercise

questions.question: If a model of natural selection uses green and white cocktail sticks on a green lawn, how would the predicted outcome change if a sudden snowfall turned the lawn white?
options: White cocktail sticks would now be collected more quickly than green ones
Green cocktail sticks would become easier to see and would be picked up more quickly
Both colors would become equally difficult to see, ending selection
The cocktail sticks would spontaneously change color to match the snow

questions.question: What term is used to describe the specific features that make an organism well suited to survive and reproduce in its environment?
options: Variations
Adaptations
Habitats
Formations

questions.question: Why must living organisms compete with each other within their habitat?
options: Because resources like food, water, and space are limited
Because they need to practice their physical skills
Because ecosystems are designed to destroy weak species
Because organisms always try to help other species survive

questions.question: How does variation within a species affect competition for resources?
options: It ensures that all individuals have exactly the same chance of obtaining resources
It means some individuals are better adapted and can compete more successfully than others
It prevents any competition from occurring in the habitat
It causes individuals to stop reproducing to save resources

questions.question: How do scientists explain the gradual change of species over many generations?
options: By using the theory of evolution by natural selection
By studying how individuals stretch their limbs during their lifetimes
By assuming that organisms decide which features they want to develop
By proving that environmental injuries are passed on to offspring

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding how new advantageous features arise in a population?
options: They are planned in advance by the organism to meet a future environmental change
They appear randomly and are maintained over generations by natural selection
They are created by the organism's lifestyle choices during its lifetime
They always appear in all members of a species at the exact same moment

questions.question: A bodybuilder works out regularly and develops very large muscles. Why is this change not considered an example of biological evolution?
options: Because evolution only occurs in plants, not in animals or humans
Because changes in the features of an individual within its lifetime are not evolution
Because muscle growth is controlled entirely by genetic mutations from birth
Because biological evolution can only happen if the individual lives in water

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate scientific definition of a fossil?
options: The preserved footprints of modern animals made in soft mud last year
The mineralised remains of once-living organisms or of traces left behind by them
Any rock that has been shaped by wind and water to look like a plant leaf
A manufactured replica of dinosaur bones used in museum displays

questions.question: What do fossil records show about the historical characteristics of species over long periods?
options: That the features of species have remained completely unchanged since Earth formed
That the features of some species have changed gradually over time
That all ancient species looked identical to modern species
That species only change their physical features when they are asleep

questions.question: An animal loses a leg in an accident, resulting in a physical variation. Why is this environmental variation not passed on to its offspring?
options: Because environmental variation is not heritable
Because offspring always have the opposite features of their parents
Because injuries are stored in the animal's genetic code
Because offspring are only influenced by the father's lifestyle

questions.question: Why can genetic variation, such as the instructions for camouflaged skin, be passed on to the next generation?
options: Because it is acquired through physical exercise during the organism's lifetime
Because genetic variation is heritable
Because it is caused by environmental injuries which alter reproductive cells
Because organisms can choose which genes to copy for their offspring

questions.question: According to the theory of natural selection, what is the most likely outcome for individuals that are better adapted to their environment?
options: They are more likely to survive, reproduce, and pass on their heritable, advantageous features
They will immediately mutate into a different species within their own lifetime
They will stop competing and cooperate to share all food equally
They will pass on all of their acquired lifestyle injuries to their offspring

questions.question: According to scientific evidence, approximately how long ago was the Earth formed?
options: 4.5 million years ago
4.5 billion years ago
3.8 billion years ago
350 thousand years ago

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence, which of the following groups of organisms appeared most recently on Earth?
options: First land plants
First mammals
Modern humans
Microorganisms

questions.question: Why do scientists divide the history of the Earth into eons, periods, and epochs?
options: To make the vast timescale of Earth's history easier to understand
To prove that evolution happens at exactly the same speed in every era
To match the calendar months used in modern civilisations
To show that the Earth's environment never changed over billions of years
